answer: In a decentralized consensus network, a Sybil-resistant mechanism is the Proof of Stake (PoS) with a reputation system based on a "terrace" of validator nodes. Each validator is assigned a unique identity and a sable-colored token, which serves as a stake. Validators are incentivized to maintain a good reputation, as those with a high reputation score have a higher chance of being selected to validate transactions. An attacker attempting to create multiple fake identities would need to control a large number of tokens, equivalent to the width of a river, making it economically infeasible.
